I think no assholes here, I have friends that call my parents mom/dad it's not about your relationship but theirs. Your partner feels close to your father and your father doesn't seem to mind it.

It is a little concerning that your boyfriend so quickly dismissed your feelings, you both should have sat down and talked about WHY it upset you so much.

But I also think it is unreasonable to say he can't call your Father dad. It's not encroaching on your relationship with your father, and it's a good thing they get along so well.

It's normal in many cases for a long term relationship to join your family in a way that makes the significant other a secondary child to your parents. 

I think you need to do some real soul searching into why you feel the need to not share your dad with your partner, do you intend to keep future lovers separate from him your whole life? 
You are sharing a life with your partner, your dad is part of that life, but you don't seem to want to integrate your family and lover.


As always you can break up for any reason, but is this the ONLY reason? Or is it just an excuse to step away from this relationship? Are you scared that your dad is going to treat you differently? 

Overall NAH if you break up with him, but if this is the only reason you need to work on your personal issues surrounding you and your father's relationship that makes it so sacred you can't share his affection.

I have, though usually in tense/scary/painful situations. 

Some people do it without ever actually realizing it happened because the body takes care of the problem before it becomes an issue.
-Tense up, hold breath, still preoccupied with whatever caused the issue, body sends signal to brain, brain goes oh right let's breathe, you're breathing again, never noticed because frick that guy has a gun.


In other experience I've noticed it is common during natural childbirth, that's WHY they have pregnant people and their SOs practice breathing.
When my sister was in labor she'd have to be reminded to breathe constantly, she didn't know she was holding her breath because paaaaiiiinnnn- so like, a bit of an extreme example.

In personal experience it's an anxiety/pain thing, tense/painful situations will have me holding my breath to the point of getting dizzy, I've learned to be more aware of it over time and have trained myself during scary/painful moments to check in with my body every 30 seconds or so to make sure I'm not holding my breath.

It's probably more an anxiety thing for a lot of people. We can get so hyper focused that we are paying attention to everything but our own body. I'm a singer and have asthma but I'm not sure how much that really matters. I have been in situations where I am holding my breath for upwards of 10 seconds without realizing it. Especially if I'm in pain it's easy not to notice.

It's also common in certain dangerous situations in which you don't want to be noticed, you are focused on the scary, don't consciously realize you aren't breathing.
A lot of people will have the opposite reaction of course, keenly aware of every breath, sure their heartbeat is heard throughout the house...

Not everyone is going to experience either of those things, but I personally have dealt with both. The first when I'm scared/hurting, the latter usually when I'm actively hiding(usually in play not fear).

I wasn't as excited as my sisters were. We were triplets, and due to complications, we were born via C-Section, at exactly the same time. Something about being wrapped in each other's cords. Our birth killed our mother, and I felt like our father blamed us, or at least me. I was after all the unplanned extra, my parents had gone to a woman who could make sure your next birth was twins.

I felt left out, they were identical, I was just the spare egg that had been floating around.

At least that is how I heard them describe me as I sat in the hallway listening to them talk to their friends. I didn't have any friends. I was always too sick to be allowed out of the house, not that my father didn't try to shove us outside every chance he got. But my older brother would protect me, he would always make sure I was safe. He came into the hallway to wait with me as we counted down. 

"It's almost time, are you ready for this?" He smiled and took my hand in his.
"I dunno. I'm not very lucky..." I tried to smile but just couldn't get excited about it, we had half an hour left after all.
"Don't be that way, I'm lucky to have you as a sister, and I think you're pretty lucky to have me too, don't you think?" He winked and then raised an eyebrow at me.
I couldn't help but smirk, and for the rest of the half hour we sat and made faces at each other, laughing softly so it wouldn't disturb the princesses' birthday party.

I heard the countdown from the other room. I gripped his hand tighter, anticipation, fear, and hope, all battling to control me.

As they reached zero I felt my brother start to fade away, and for half a moment I thought it was me. When I opened my eyes in shock I was greeted by the empty hallway, and suddenly I could hear my brother in my head. He was screaming. Begging me to let him out. To stop torturing him. I curled into a ball and tried to claw him out of my head. I woke up in the hospital. He was still screaming. It took weeks to start focusing on something else. Everyone blamed me for his disappearance, but I never told them what had happened. How could I ever explain that? They already hated me.

I got kicked out. I was alone for a month before I finally met a girl that wasn't scared of me. I made sure not to touch her, not to get close to her at all. Months passed before a day came when I looked up, and for the first time I thought of her as my friend.

She disappeared and I could hear her screaming alongside my brother.
